source.title: On the Convergence of AdaBound and its Connection to SGD

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Compares an adaptive optimizer with momentum SGD on CIFAR test accuracy, using AdaBound rather than the adaptive methods named in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports a stochastic convex convergence counterexample and regret analysis; these do not test a mapped version. Cited findings about Adam and generalization are prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out image-classification accuracy of AdaBound and momentum SGD, bearing on V4 with a different adaptive optimizer and a dampening comparison. Its convex convergence results do not test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical conclusion: dampened SGDM performs competitively with AdaBound on CIFAR, with broader evaluation left open. The paper also disproves the previously stated AdaBound regret guarantee and supplies a corrected guarantee under different assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: Tests AdaBound and dampened SGDM on CIFAR-10 with the reported setup, rather than the Adam/SGD comparisons in V4; limited to one network and dataset.
record.method_sensitivity: AdaBound's γ setting changes training and final test performance: γ = 10⁻¹⁰ degrades performance relative to γ = 0.001, while γ = 100 shows no significant difference from γ = 0.001 throughout training. SGDM dampening κ = β₁ changes its performance substantially relative to κ = 0.

fits_no_version.finding: Very small AdaBound γ degrades training and test performance; γ = 0.001 and γ = 100 perform similarly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AdaBound's performance depends on how quickly its learning-rate bounds approach the SGD limit.

record.problems: The empirical comparison is limited to one Wide ResNet and CIFAR-10; the authors say extensive experiments are out of scope. Several curve results are reported only as figures, without exact values. The reported standard deviations concern the bias-correction comparison, not the primary AdaBound versus SGDM comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible outcomes beyond the extracted CIFAR-10 optimizer comparisons. Convex convergence proofs and cited prior-study results do not measure a version's mapped behavior.

untested.parts: Adam itself, language benchmarks, systematic limited-versus-broad tuning, decoupled weight decay, explicit switching from Adam to SGD, and equal-or-better training performance accompanying worse test performance.
Batch-size effects and remedies under fixed epoch budgets.

missing.what: AdaBound versus ordinary SGDM with κ = 0, together with the improvement from setting κ = β₁. Figure 1 shows the optimizer ranking depends on dampening; exact endpoint values are not stated.
missing.locator: Section 5, Figure 1 and discussion of equations 23–24

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. The experiment reuses specified hyperparameters rather than conducting a systematic tuning-budget comparison. The 0.11-point accuracy difference alone does not establish a statistically reliable optimizer disadvantage.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adam comparisons across image and language benchmarks; limited versus broad hyperparameter tuning; weight decay and switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons and fixed-epoch large-batch penalties.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet-28-2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AdaBound, γ = 10⁻³, and compared with SGDM using κ = β₁.
rows.note: The authors describe SGDM as slightly outperforming AdaBound; the small difference does not show adaptive optimization generalizing worse in this comparison.
rows.check: AdaBound is 0.11 percentage points worse than dampened SGDM, so 'absent' incorrectly discards a small difference in the predicted direction. The authors describe competitive performance; no significance test for this difference is reported.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet-28-2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AdaBound, γ = 10⁻¹⁰, compared with AdaBound at γ = 10⁻³.
rows.note: The text says γ = 10⁻¹⁰ causes noticeable degradation in final test performance relative to γ = 10⁻³; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: This compares two AdaBound settings without an SGD baseline. It establishes sensitivity to γ, but cannot independently establish V4's adaptive-versus-SGD effect. Both training accuracy and final test performance deteriorate.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet-28-2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AdaBound at γ = 10⁻³ and γ = 100.
rows.note: The authors report no significant difference throughout training between γ = 0.001 and γ = 100; precise values are not stated.
rows.check: This compares two AdaBound settings without an SGD baseline. Their reported similarity does not establish absence of V4's optimizer difference.

relationships.condition: Wide ResNet-28-2 on CIFAR-10; AdaBound γ = 0.001 versus SGDM with κ = β₁
relationships.reason: R1 shows near parity: 93.90% versus 94.01% mean test accuracy over five runs. The adaptive disadvantage is small with this SGDM configuration.
relationships.display_finding: Reported mean accuracy of 93.90% for AdaBound versus SGDM's 94.01% remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Same network and dataset; undampened versus dampened SGDM
relationships.reason: The text and Figure 1 show AdaBound outperforming undampened SGDM, while dampening brings SGDM to competitive performance. The optimizer ranking depends on the momentum update choice; this comparison is missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Reported AdaBound superiority over undampened SGDM and competitive dampened SGDM performance remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: Wide ResNet-28-2 on CIFAR-10; AdaBound versus SGDM with κ = β₁
